publisher: UK Visas and Immigration (Home Office), GOV.UK
raw_extract:
You may be able to settle permanently in the UK if you have one of the following visas:

-   Skilled Worker, Health and Care Worker or Tier 2 (General)
-   T2 Minister of Religion or Tier 2 (Minister of Religion)
-   International Sportsperson, T2 Sportsperson or Tier 2 (Sportsperson)

Indefinite leave to remain is how you settle in the UK. It’s also called ‘settlement’.

## Eligibility

You must:

-   have lived and worked in the UK for 5 years - there are rules for what [counts towards your time in the UK](/indefinite-leave-to-remain-tier-2-t2-skilled-worker-visa/time-uk)
-   meet the [salary requirements](/indefinite-leave-to-remain-tier-2-t2-skilled-worker-visa/salary-requirements)
-   continue to be needed for your job and meet the salary requirements after you get indefinite leave to remain - you’ll need a document from your employer (sponsor) to confirm this

## When to apply

The earliest you can apply is 28 days before you’ve been in the UK for 5 years on a qualifying visa.

## Fees and how long it takes

It costs £3,226 for each person applying.
research_notes: The UK settlement route is officially called 'Indefinite leave to remain' (ILR). The minimum qualifying period on the main work route is 5 years. CRITICAL for a student-corpus: the 5 years is a requirement to 'have lived AND worked in the UK'. Time on a Student visa is not time on a qualifying route, and the Graduate visa is likewise not listed among the qualifying visas on this page. So a student's realistic ILR timeline is 5 years of Skilled Worker, not 5 years total from arrival - a student arriving at 19 would not be eligible before roughly age 24+ and would need to qualify for Skilled Worker in the interim. Supporting figure from the same research pass: Skilled Worker requires a salary of at least £41,700 per year (or the going rate for the job, whichever is higher), so the work route also imposes a substantial earnings bar. Fee recorded: £3,226 per person.

claims.statement: The UK permanent residence route is officially 'Indefinite leave to remain' (ILR), and on the Skilled Worker route you must have lived and worked in the UK for 5 years.
ILR also requires you to meet the salary requirements and to remain needed for your job after settlement, evidenced by a document from your sponsor.
An ILR application costs £3,226 per person, and the earliest it can be filed is 28 days before completing the 5-year qualifying period.
The Skilled Worker visa that precedes ILR requires pay of at least £41,700 per year, or the going rate for the occupation, whichever is higher.
